chapter.title: Part V: Extend what the work can do with Skills
chapter.body_html:
Part V covers all 24 of pstack's Skills.

!

You can skip this part. I recommend reading only the chapters you care about.

You can read the source of each Skill at any time in the pstack repository. When you need one, look up the matching chapter and file.

What Part V tells you

Part V answers the following questions about each Skill.

  • What each Skill does and when to use it. For example, /how explains what the current code does before you change it.
  • What shape of output it returns. For example, /why labels each reason it finds with a level that says whether a record backs it or it is a guess.
  • Example requests that call it directly, and how to choose between similar Skills. For example, use /interrogate to look for weak points inside the diff, and /blast-radius to look for what breaks outside the diff.

A Skill packages the steps of a task under a name, so that each call by that name runs the same steps. The tasks include, for example, investigating with /why, designing with /architect, verifying with /blast-radius, and cleaning up with /unslop.

/poteto-mode calls most of them automatically, as steps of a Playbook.

The user can also call a Skill directly by name. The user calls one directly when they want to change the Skill choice the Playbook made, or when they want a more careful check than the default.

For example, say the diff is small enough that the /poteto-mode steps do not call /blast-radius, but you do not fully trust the diff. You can call /blast-radius directly and verify what that diff could break.

To call a Skill directly, the user needs to know what it does. The chapters of Part V explain what each Skill does.

The chapters in this part

Chapter Role Skills covered
Chapter 22: Understand the codebase and past work Investigate what the current code does and why it has its current shape, and resume where the last session stopped /how, /why, /teach, /recall
Chapter 23: Design a Playbook for work that no Playbook fits For work that no Playbook fits, design a procedure that fixes the finish condition and the verification setup first /figure-it-out
Chapter 24: Run agents in parallel and compare designs and artifacts Fix the types and module boundaries before implementation, have several agents solve the same problem and compare the results, and split work across several agents /architect, /arena, /swarm
Chapter 25: Extend pstack to your own way of working and to Grok Bot Build a mode Skill for one user from that user's chat history, and build a page that starts Grok Bot with a button /automate-me, /make-bot-ui
Chapter 26: Build verification and keep it current as the app changes Build a project-specific Skill, called a verification skill, that runs the app along the same path a user takes, and fix it as the app changes /create-verification-skill, /maintain-verification-skill
Chapter 27: Check what a change could break and where the diff is weak Look for what could break outside the changed files, and have several models look for weak points in the diff /blast-radius, /interrogate
Chapter 28: Record decisions and leave evidence for long agent runs Record decisions and their grounds, and have a model from a different family review them /show-me-your-work
Chapter 29: Keep code quality with 16 TypeScript rules Make invalid states impossible to write in the types, and validate outside data once, at the place it enters /typescript-best-practices
Chapter 30: TDD: verify with a failing test before the fix Before you fix a bug, write a test that fails before the fix /tdd
Chapter 31: Remove comments and tidy the codebase Have an agent that did not write the diff review its unneeded comments, and delete them /no-comments
Chapter 32: Keep writing quality high Remove AI habits from prose, restate a hard-to-follow reply without jargon, and pick the kind of document before you write /unslop, /bro, /technical-writing
Chapter 33: Reflect on what the work taught you and apply it Keep what a long task taught, for example by adding it to an existing Skill /reflect
Chapter 34: Install pstack and choose a model for each role Install pstack and set the model pstack uses for each role /setup-pstack
Chapter 35: /poteto-mode is pstack's Router Lay out the rules that pick the Playbook that fits a request and load the Skills and Principles it needs /poteto-mode

This book orders the chapters along the flow of the work. The flow is as follows.

  • Understand the current code (Chapter 22)
  • Run several agents in parallel and compare designs and artifacts (Chapter 24)
  • Implement, and verify that the implementation works (Chapter 26)
  • Verify what the change could break (Chapter 27)
  • Record decisions (Chapter 28)
  • Clean up the code (Chapters 29 to 31)
  • Clean up the prose (Chapter 32)
  • Keep what you learned (Chapter 33)

Chapter 23 covers the Skill that designs the way of working itself, for work that no Playbook fits. That Skill deals with how the whole task proceeds, not with one step in the flow. So this book treats it apart from the flow.

Chapter 25 collects two Skills that extend pstack to fit the user's habits and to work with Grok Bot. Neither Skill belongs to a particular step in the flow, so this book treats them apart from the flow.

Chapter 34 covers /setup-pstack, which sets the models. Chapter 35 covers /poteto-mode, which receives the request first.

The pstack README sums up how to get started as "pick models with /setup-pstack, and use /poteto-mode for work that requires rigor. That's it." The README also says that /poteto-mode uses the other Skills as needed.

/setup-pstack is the first Skill you use when you start with pstack, and /poteto-mode is the first Skill you use each time you start a task. Neither Skill belongs to a particular step in the flow, so this book covers them in chapters apart from the flow.

Quick reference for all Skills

Skill Summary When to use it Who calls it Chapter
/how Explains what the current code does: what triggers the work, which functions it passes through, and how the data flows When the user or the agent wants to know how a subsystem behaves before a code change, or asks where code should live /poteto-mode calls it in the "Non-negotiables" rules and in the steps of Playbooks such as "Investigation", "Bug fix", "Feature", and "Refactoring". /teach, /architect, /no-comments, and the user also call it Chapter 22
/why Investigates why the code has its current shape from records such as commits, PRs, and tickets, and answers with the reasons that a record backs, kept apart from guesses When the user or the agent asks about the reason for a design, the history of a regression, or the origin of a threshold /poteto-mode calls it in the steps of the "Investigation" and "Bug fix" Playbooks. /teach, /recall, /architect, /no-comments, and the user also call it Chapter 22
/teach Calls /how and /why, and combines what the code or change is, how it works, and why it was built that way into one plain explanation When a summary is not enough and the user wants to understand a change or a subsystem in depth Only when the user calls it by name Chapter 22
/recall Gathers the history of recent work from your own chat history and shared records, and returns a short note on how far the work got and what to do next When the user wants to know where the last session stopped, before they start or resume work Only when the user calls it by name Chapter 22
/blast-radius Looks for what could break outside the changed files, and runs the code to verify the grounds for calling the change safe When the user wants to know what else a diff could break, for a diff that looks small but that they do not fully trust Only when the user calls it by name Chapter 27
/interrogate Has reviewers on different models look for weak points in the same diff, and the main agent sorts their findings into four groups When the user or the agent wants several models to look for where a diff breaks, strict code-quality concerns included /poteto-mode calls it in the "Non-negotiables" rule that applies before a contested design merges, and in the steps of the "Feature" and "Opening a PR" Playbooks. /architect and the user also call it Chapter 27
/figure-it-out For work that no Playbook fits, designs a procedure that fixes the finish condition and the verification setup first and keeps a record of decisions as it goes When the user hands off a migration that spans many call sites or work to continue while they are away, or when no Playbook fits the request /poteto-mode calls it through the rules in the "Playbooks" section, which send large work, away-from-desk work, and work that no Playbook fits to this Skill. The user also calls it Chapter 23
/architect Before the agent writes code that crosses function boundaries, it fixes the types, function signatures, and module boundaries in a skeleton with no function bodies When the agent is about to write code that crosses function boundaries /poteto-mode calls it in the "Non-negotiables" rules and in the steps of the "Feature", "Bug fix", "Refactoring", and "Perf issue" Playbooks. /figure-it-out, /no-comments, and the user also call it Chapter 24
/arena Has N candidates solve the same problem in parallel, picks the best candidate as the base, and ports the good ideas from the others When the user or the agent builds an artifact that is costly to change later, such as the format of a cache key /poteto-mode calls it in the "Non-negotiables" rules and in the steps of the "Feature", "Eval", and "Orchestrate" Playbooks. /architect, /blast-radius, and the user also call it Chapter 24
/swarm Runs N Workers in parallel that either split the work or compete, and combines their results into one report When the agent splits work in parallel for coverage, competition, a gate, or a divided search /poteto-mode calls it in the "Non-negotiables" rules and in the steps of the "Multi-phase or multi-PR plan" and "Autopilot-full" Playbooks. The user also calls it Chapter 24
/automate-me Builds a -mode Skill for one user from that user's chat history and answers to questions When the user wants the agent to follow a mode Skill that fits their preferences and way of working Only when the user calls it by name Chapter 25
/make-bot-ui Builds a page whose button starts Grok Bot over a webhook, without showing the sender key to the agent When the user wants to build a page that starts Grok Bot over a webhook, provide the sender key, and expose the page on Tailscale Only when the user calls it by name Chapter 25
/create-verification-skill Generates a project-specific verification skill in .cursor/skills/verify-<app>/ that starts and drives the app and keeps evidence When the user's project has no scripted way to prove the app's behavior again and again The user calls it. /setup-pstack also calls it in its last step, which offers to generate a verification skill, when the user accepts Chapter 26
/maintain-verification-skill Checks whether the verification skill and the Feature Map disagree with the current app, and fixes the drift When the user has changed the app and wants to fix the drift between the Feature Map and the current app Only when the user calls it by name Chapter 26
/show-me-your-work Records the decisions and grounds of a long task in decisions.tsv, and has a model from a different family review that record When the agent runs a long task, an autonomous task, or a task the user checks later after stepping away /poteto-mode calls it in the "Non-negotiables" rules and in the steps of Playbooks such as "Autonomous run", "Orchestrate", "Hillclimb", and "Autopilot-full". /figure-it-out and the user also call it Chapter 28
/typescript-best-practices Shows, in sixteen TypeScript rules, how to make invalid states impossible to write in the types When the agent reads or edits a .ts or .tsx file Loads automatically when the agent reads or writes a .ts or .tsx file. The user does not need to call it by name Chapter 29
/tdd Writes one regression test before the agent fixes a bug, and verifies that the test fails before the fix and passes after it When the user asks for TDD or a failing test, or when a test that runs locally right away can verify the bug /poteto-mode calls it in step 5 of the "Bug fix" Playbook. The user also calls it Chapter 30
/no-comments Has Comment Sicko, a subagent that did not write the comments, review the comments in the diff, and fixes the findings it accepts When the agent removes comments from the diff before review /poteto-mode calls it in the "Non-negotiables" rules and in the steps of the "Opening a PR", "Autopilot-full", "Autopilot-stack", and "Multi-phase or multi-PR plan" Playbooks. The user also calls it Chapter 31
/unslop Uses numbered rules to remove, from any prose, the habits that show an AI wrote it When the agent writes any prose, replies included /poteto-mode calls it in the "Non-negotiables" rules and in the steps of the "Investigation", "Opening a PR", and "Multi-phase or multi-PR plan" Playbooks. /technical-writing, /show-me-your-work, /recall, /teach, /blast-radius, /automate-me, and the user also call it Chapter 32
/bro Restates the agent's last reply without jargon When the agent's reply is detailed but the user cannot tell what it says Only when the user calls it by name Chapter 32
/technical-writing Sets the standard for writing technical documents in four layers, from the kind of document down to how to write one sentence When the agent writes or reviews docs, RFCs, READMEs, PR descriptions, or commit messages /poteto-mode calls it in the "Non-negotiables" rules and in the steps of the "Opening a PR" and "Multi-phase or multi-PR plan" Playbooks. The user also calls it Chapter 32
/reflect Pulls lessons that carry over to the next task out of the conversation, and keeps only the ones the user approves, for example by adding them to an existing Skill When the user calls /reflect right after a task that taught something Only when the user calls it by name Chapter 33
/setup-pstack Asks for the reasoning budget and the model for each role, and writes the answers to the always-applied rule ~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc When the user starts using pstack, or wants to change the model pstack uses for a role The user. SKILL.md has no disable-model-invocation: true, so the agent can also pick and run it from the content of a request, such as "configure pstack models" Chapter 34
/poteto-mode Collects the rules that pick the Playbook that fits a request and have the agent load the Skills and Principles it needs When the user requests work that needs rigor, such as work where the agent reproduces a bug before it fixes it and verifies that the fix works Only when the user calls it by name. Once called, it stays in effect for later turns of the same conversation until the user says to stop Chapter 35
